name: Falling Fruit
description: An open-source, crowd-mapped atlas of urban fruit trees and forageable plants. LA has thousands of loquat, fig, and citrus trees on public land.

name: iNaturalist
description: Photograph a plant, bug, or bird on your camping trip and the community helps identify it. Observations feed open biodiversity data used by scientists.

name: OpenStreetMap
description: The Wikipedia of maps. Trail and campground data you can download, edit, and use offline in apps like Organic Maps.

name: Organic Maps
description: A free, private offline maps app built on OpenStreetMap. Useful when you lose cell signal in Joshua Tree or the Sierra.

name: Recreation Information Database (RIDB)
description: The federal open-data API behind Recreation.gov, with campgrounds, facilities, and activities. Good raw material for building on top of this site.

name: Open Food Facts
description: A collaborative, open database of food products and ingredients, with the data, apps, and API all openly licensed.

name: Calflora
description: Observation data on California's wild plants. Use it to track spring wildflower blooms in Anza-Borrego and Carrizo Plain.

name: Mealie
description: A self-hosted recipe manager and meal planner. Import the recipes on this site and plan a week around the market.
